content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I recently resolved some network issues with [product_name] and [product_name] software. Now, I am stuck trying to add [product_name] as equipment in [product_name] engineering platform. Any tips? I have downloaded the latest [product_name] platform, but it only includes [version_no] controllers, not [product_name].
Hi, This discussion might help: Setting up communication between [product_name] ([article_no]) and [version_no].
Programming [product_name] must be done using [product_name] software, which is standalone and not integrated into [product_name] engineering platform. Thankfully.
This topic pertains to making communication work between [product_name] and [version_no], not migration or integration.

You want to add [product_name] as a device in the network view of [version_no], correct? [product_name] can't be chosen as a device here, but that's not necessary for programming or networking to work. Refer to the previously mentioned discussion for help. By the way, this is more of an engineering platform question than strictly a [product_name] question.

In my view, the original poster wishes to select [product_name] in the engineering platform like the [version_no]. This is not possible and, thankfully, the [product_name] software continues as a separate tool.

I also hope [product_name] software remains independent from integration with the engineering platform. The engineering platform is too resource-heavy and expensive to justify merging for smaller applications.
You can't add [product_name] hardware for configuration or programming in the engineering platform – that's simply not an option.

Hi, If you wish for [product_name] integration in the engineering platform, maybe it'll happen in a future version. However, I doubt [company_name] will do this, since the engineering platform requires substantial computing power and licensing, which makes little sense for small devices like [product_name].

Why do you need this? You can already connect [product_name] to a panel using networking. You can create scripts for the panel in the engineering platform referencing [product_name] tags. Personally, I think the [product_name] software should have an interface similar to the engineering platform, but that's just my opinion.
Oh, I don't need this—the original poster does. Personally, I have no need for it.

Hello, To my knowledge, there are no plans to allow programming of [product_name] using the engineering platform. However, with [product_name] software you can: In network mode, you add [product_name] and a compatible controller. Then you access the properties of the controller. Inside the dialog, there's a section for the engineering tool, where you choose the related project. If you double-click the controller, the engineering platform opens with the associated program. Remember, this is a feature of the [product_name] software, not the engineering platform itself. Hope this clarifies things.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are uncertain and sometimes frustrated about not being able to add [product_name] modules directly in the [product_name] engineering platform, hoping for integration as with other controllers. Community members clarify that [product_name] programming is handled by a separate standalone tool and has never been part of the engineering platform. Some users value this independence, citing ease of use and reduced system requirements, while others speculate about possible future harmonization or beneficial integration.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to be able to add, configure, and program the [product_name] module within the [product_name] engineering platform, similar to other controllers, and seeks seamless integration between [product_name] devices and [company_name]'s central engineering environment.
